body:
Local saves, export/import and rewind for the approved anonymous NES multiplayer release. This is a bounded outcome under epic #2, not authorization to skip its dependencies.

## Requirements

- Parent epic: #2; stable plan ID: `D06`.
- Priority: **P2: retained progress**. Priority orders eligible work only.
- Source: [approved plan snapshot](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/blob/ecf6bd4c7443526f0a163b721a351c854ee90fd4/docs/implementation/browser-nes-audit.md), row D06; design saves.
- Governing [design](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/blob/ecf6bd4c7443526f0a163b721a351c854ee90fd4/docs/design/browser-nes-platform.md), [UI](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/blob/ecf6bd4c7443526f0a163b721a351c854ee90fd4/docs/design/browser-nes-ui.md), and [architecture/delivery](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/blob/ecf6bd4c7443526f0a163b721a351c854ee90fd4/docs/implementation/browser-nes-platform.md).
- User approved reviewed head `2e8adfcd3259f5bdffdc9a13ef9b983f78cfb965` and explicitly requested merge/start; [planning PR #3](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/pull/3) merged as `ecf6bd4c7443526f0a163b721a351c854ee90fd4`.

## Observable acceptance

Persistence/error/export evidence, compatible restore and 10-second/32 MiB rewind; no cloud/ROM persistence. AC-07; S12/S14–17.

## Rewind measurement carried from D02

The ten-second requirement is elapsed emulated time, not a universal fixed 600-frame count. For the selected NTSC rate of approximately 60.0988 frames/s, retain at least 601 frame intervals (602 snapshots if storing both endpoints). Derive the span from the actual emulation rate, for example `ceil(frame_rate * 10)`, and qualify other supported regions at their own rates. Verify actual retained allocations remain within32 MiB and that replay after rewind matches; do not substitute a multiplication of wire-checkpoint size for the implemented local buffer accounting. This clarifies the existing AC-07 target and does not expand scope or change dependencies.

## Dependencies and ownership

- Blocks on: [D05 #9](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/issues/9).
- Original dependency scope: D05.
- Status: In progress. D05 merged as f248296; root integration preflight passed in 6.26s. Controls are accepted pending CI; builder capacity is now assigned to the safe local save boundary first.
- Builder: /root/d04_foundation. Work branch: feat/d06-saves; owned worktree: /tmp/retro-d06-saves. Dispatcher: root orchestrator.
- Delivery board: https://github.com/orgs/TuringTestee/projects/1 . Issues own acceptance, dependencies and ownership; the board reflects them.

## Boundaries and delivery

No new accounts, user-ROM sharing/storage, server gameplay, streaming fallback, recording, or unapproved scope. Reuse approved architecture and existing assets; leave bounded implementation details to the builder. Source plans hold rationale; this issue owns live acceptance, blockers and ownership.

Use issue-resolver in an isolated worktree, focused tests and README preflight, bounded CI, and independent local review. Follow epic #2’s explicit policy B authorization: the implementation agent may merge after current-head local review acceptance and passing required checks, respecting branch protections. Do not request per-PR approval again; verify integration before releasing dependent work. Completion requires acceptance/integration evidence, not merely an issue closure. Link implementation PRs to this child issue without closing epic #2.

## Implementation order and reuse audit

Build a safe save format before persistence UI. The integrated demo proves in-memory save/replay, but does not yet provide a validated persistent/exportable state interface. This clarifies existing D06 scope; dependencies and product acceptance are unchanged.

Source audit: main `e2f43f97feb0277e62f4fbdb4c4f63335f5ee4d6`, `spikes/d02/src/local_player.rs`, `checkpoint.rs`, `memory_tail.rs`, and the pinned upstream state/memory implementation. The local-player ABI has no byte export/import or battery interface. The experimental checkpoint codec is NROM/NTSC-only and removes mapper state; merely dropping its admission guard would corrupt other mapper restores. Upstream mutable-memory serialization is useful reuse, but is not by itself whole-state export/import safety.

- [ ] First implement the versioned local save boundary with exact ROM/core/schema/settings identity, bounded allocations/fields, locally reconstructed immutable cartridge mappings, mutable mapper state and corrupted-CPU flag preservation. D06 owns this reusable validation/schema layer; later peer code must use only its audited supported subset, never generic upstream deserialization.
- [ ] Expose validated save and battery-state APIs, then IndexedDB persistence and import/export with visible error handling. Invalid imports leave the live game unchanged; no ROM content is exported.
- [ ] Implement measured rewind using actual emulated timing. Existing `local_fps()` rounds to 60/50 and must not establish the ten-second bound. Count actual retained allocations; use sparse checkpoints plus input replay or measured deltas if needed to meet the unchanged 32 MiB budget.
- [ ] Prove representative bank-changing, RAM/battery and regional cases, malformed imports and post-restore replay. Header-only mapper boot tests are insufficient.

D20 remains the downstream broad qualification gate and must not become a dependency of D06 (that would create a cycle). Keep intermediate PRs bounded and reviewed; an NROM-only intermediate result does not close D06 or reduce the agreed hardware scope. If evidence forces reduced support or relaxed rewind guarantees, return for user alignment.


## Current delivery checkpoint
Battery boundary integrated through PR47 at564bc37 after independent acceptance and all seven CI jobs passing13m15s; exact combined tree verified, integration preflight11.57s. D06 remains open. /root/d04_foundation now owns remaining validated whole-state codec/persistence/rewind preparation in feat/d06-state, /tmp/retro-d06-state. Keep bounded reviewed slices; no hardware scope reduction.

comments.body:
Read-only preparation confirms that D06 should begin with the validated local save boundary, then add persistence and rewind. This refines implementation evidence without changing acceptance or dependencies; no D06 code was started before D05 integration.

Inspected pinned TetaNES `a0a6b17f8ba9c5ee451453fb2409753fd06e5a31` and the integrated local/checkpoint adapters:

- `tetanes-core/src/memory.rs:173–248` already excludes immutable ROM from snapshots but allocates untrusted `state.len` during decode. Reconstruct cartridge-derived geometry locally and admit only an exact bounded mutable tail before typed decode.
- `control_deck.rs:657` restores through `load_bus`, reconstructs local ROM and mapper mappings. Retain exact SHA-256/core/schema/resolved-settings identity; upstream CRC32/layout comparison alone is insufficient.
- `control_deck.rs:1073` ignores trailing state bytes and clears input. The application boundary must reject trailing data and preserve the promised replay behavior explicitly.
- `control_deck.rs:909/933` and `bus.rs:600/634` expose battery APIs including mapper extensions, but `set_sram` silently accepts mismatched lengths. Validate exact identity/length before mutation.
- The 24 mapper variants require real dynamic-state validation. MMC1 partial serial writes, MMC3 banks/mirroring/IRQ/A12 state and Bandai optional EEPROM/barcode state are representative pitfalls. EEPROM `rom_data` is mutable battery data despite its name; initial-template equality would incorrectly reject valid changes.
- Keep the NROM/NTSC peer codec unchanged. A separate bounded local codec should stage a candidate Bus, validate timing/input/mapper invariants and explicit CPU-corruption state, then commit transactionally through `load_bus`.
- Derive rewind from actual emulated duration using region clock/frame-cycle accounting, not rounded FPS. Measure retained allocations under the existing 32 MiB/literal 10-second requirement.

Meaningful tests: bank-changing/partial-write/IRQ replay, RAM and battery extensions, CPU corruption, PAL/Dendy timing, exact identity mismatch, oversized layout, trailing data, malformed fields and unchanged live state after rejection; check exports against distinctive immutable ROM patterns. Partial mapper support may be an intermediate reviewed slice, never closure or silently reduced D06 scope.

[Authoritative upstream source](https://github.com/lukexor/tetanes/tree/a0a6b17f8ba9c5ee451453fb2409753fd06e5a31/tetanes-core/src). This is a code audit, not claimed runtime proof.
